text:
Bo Horvat is the Islanders' captain, their first-line center and, lately, the guy Pete DeBoer reaches for when nothing else works. DeBoer put him back with Mathew Barzal last week, and Horvat won the game against St. Louis in a shootout.

The goals have been slow: nine on 11.4 expected goals (the quality of his chances), and just two in his last ten games despite taking seven shots in San Jose and piling up chances in Detroit. That's the kind of gap that usually closes. He's shooting 12%, a bit below his normal, and our range has him finishing with 26 to 42 goals.

The worry sits at the other end. The players our numbers say he plays like share one trait: chances against pile up with him on the ice. Evolving-Hockey notes he faces the other team's best every night, which explains some of it. Stefen Rosner of NHL.com flagged a few missed backchecks in Friday's loss to Winnipeg, calling it "Uncharacteristic of Horvat." With Matthew Schaefer quieter lately, New York needs its captain's goals to show up soon.
